blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Debates about the future of work have been running, with varying degrees of seriousness, for more than a decade. The pandemic accelerated many trends that would otherwise have taken another fifteen years to mature — hybrid working, digital collaboration, distributed teams across time zones, and a re-examination of the basic assumption that productive work requires a shared physical space.

What has become clear, with the benefit of a few years of data, is that no single model is universally superior. Some roles lose very little through remote work. Others, especially those dependent on tacit learning, informal mentoring and cross-functional collaboration, pay a real if hard-to-measure cost. Thoughtful organisations are rejecting the ideological debate — remote versus office — in favour of a more granular question: which activities benefit from proximity, and when, exactly?

The deeper shift may be cultural rather than physical. For the first time in generations, a significant proportion of professionals are openly questioning the centrality of paid work in their lives. HR functions that rise to this moment will be those that help organisations earn people's attention and commitment — rather than assume them. In a world where mediocre employers are easier than ever to identify and avoid, the cost of complacency has quietly become extraordinary.

items.q: According to the text, what has a few years of data made clear about the models of work?
options: No single model is universally superior
The office model has been fully discredited
Remote work is superior for every role
Hybrid work always outperforms the alternatives
items.why: "no single model is universally superior" — nenhum modelo vence em todos os casos.

items.q: Which kind of work, according to the text, pays a real if hard-to-measure cost when done remotely?
options: Routine transactional processing
Work dependent on tacit learning and informal mentoring
Standardised reporting
Individual analytical tasks
items.why: "those dependent on tacit learning, informal mentoring and cross-functional collaboration, pay a real… cost".

items.q: The author suggests that thoughtful organisations are replacing the 'remote versus office' debate with…
options: a permanent freeze on any change
a granular question about which activities benefit from proximity
a company-wide mandate to return to the office
a decision made purely by cost
items.why: "in favour of a more granular question: which activities benefit from proximity, and when".

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: There is one correct answer to remote versus office that applies to all firms
The right approach depends on the specific activity
The deeper change may be cultural rather than physical
Distance carries costs that are real but hard to measure
items.why: Inferência: o texto rejeita a busca por um modelo único e ideológico — logo discordaria de uma resposta universal.

items.q: The final line — "the cost of complacency has quietly become extraordinary" — suggests that…
options: complacency has always carried the same price
the cost of hiring has fallen sharply
employers who fail to earn commitment will lose people to better options
employers can now afford to relax their standards
items.why: Inferência: se empregadores medíocres são fáceis de identificar e evitar, a acomodação sai caro — perde-se talento.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry encerrando o offsite. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So — two days, a great deal of debate, and I think we can close on something more useful than a slogan. If there is one line I would ask you to take away, it is this: we are done arguing about remote versus office. That framing has cost us eighteen months and settled nothing.

Instead, we agreed to treat proximity as a tool. For onboarding, for tacit learning, for the messy cross-functional work where nobody quite knows the answer yet — being in the same room earns its keep. For focused, individual output, it frequently does not. The task now is to be honest, activity by activity, about where that line actually falls.

The point I want to leave you with is harder. For the first time in my career, a real share of our best people are quietly asking whether work deserves the place it holds in their lives. We will not win that argument by mandate. We earn their commitment, or we lose it to an employer who bothered to.

So my ask is simple. Let's stop trying to predict the future of work, and start earning it — one honest decision at a time.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is the one line Harry asks the committee to take away?
options: That everyone should return to the office full time
That they are done arguing about remote versus office
That remote work has proven superior
That the offsite reached no conclusion at all
items.why: "we are done arguing about remote versus office."

items.q: How does Harry propose the organisation should treat proximity?
options: As an ideology to defend
As a tool, useful for some activities and not others
As an outdated concept to abandon
As a cost to be eliminated
items.why: "we agreed to treat proximity as a tool" — útil para onboarding e trabalho tácito, menos para output individual.

items.q: According to Harry, what are a real share of the best people quietly asking?
options: Whether the office will reopen
Whether their pay is competitive
Whether work deserves the place it holds in their lives
Whether the company will merge
items.why: "a real share of our best people are quietly asking whether work deserves the place it holds in their lives."

items.q: When Harry says "That framing has cost us eighteen months and settled nothing," he implies that…
options: the binary debate wasted time without resolving anything
eighteen months was too short to decide
the decision was made quickly and cleanly
the remote-versus-office debate was a productive use of time
items.why: Inferência: o enquadramento binário consumiu tempo e não produziu decisão — por isso ele o abandona.

items.q: What does Harry's closing ask — "stop trying to predict the future of work, and start earning it" — reveal about his view?
options: The future is fixed and only needs forecasting
HR should focus on producing accurate forecasts
Commitment must be won through action, not assumed or predicted
The company should wait for the market to decide
items.why: Inferência: prever é passivo; "earn it" implica conquistar compromisso com decisões concretas, não presumi-lo.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Much of what juniors absorb comes through tacit learning — watching a senior handle a difficult client." Tacit learning is…
options: a written onboarding manual
knowledge picked up informally through observation and practice
a formal certification programme
learning delivered exclusively online
items.why: Tacit learning = aprendizagem tácita: o que se absorve implicitamente, sem instrução formal.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Rather than a blanket rule, we need a more ___ view — activity by activity, team by team."
options: distributed
granular
complacent
ideological
items.why: Granular = detalhado, caso a caso — o oposto de uma regra genérica.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The desk runs as a ___, with members in London, Singapore and São Paulo working across time zones."
options: cost of mediocrity
ideological debate
centrality of work
distributed team
items.why: Distributed team = equipe distribuída, espalhada por fusos e locais diferentes.

items.q: "The danger is complacency — assuming good people will stay simply because they always have." Complacency is…
options: a formal grievance process
excessive caution about risk
open conflict between teams
self-satisfied inaction and a false sense of security
items.why: Complacency = complacência: acomodação, presumir que está tudo bem sem agir.

items.q: "For the first time, many professionals are questioning the centrality of work in their lives." This phrase refers to…
options: the location of the head office
the number of hours in a contract
the central place work holds relative to everything else
the seniority of a role
items.why: Centrality of work = centralidade do trabalho: quão central o trabalho é na vida da pessoa.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em debates sobre o futuro do trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Being in the same room for onboarding really earns its keep." To earn its keep means to…
options: justify its cost through the value it delivers
be difficult to measure
become mandatory by policy
take up too much time
items.why: Earn its keep = valer o que custa, justificar-se pelo valor entregue.

items.q: "We can't fix engagement by mandate." Doing something by mandate means…
options: by imposing it as a top-down rule
by outsourcing it
by trial and error
by voluntary agreement
items.why: By mandate = por imposição/ordem de cima, não por adesão espontânea.

items.q: "Several managers pushed back on the return-to-office policy." They…
options: resisted or challenged it
forgot to read it
approved it immediately
rewrote the whole thing
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar por completo.

items.q: "None of these perks will move the needle on retention." This means they will…
options: cost far too much
not make a noticeable difference
upset the finance team
take years to approve
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir diferença perceptível.

items.q: "We keep launching initiatives but never follow through on them." To follow through means to…
options: cancel it quietly
carry something to completion
delegate it upwards
announce it publicly
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi iniciado.
